correctness.rationale: In characteristic p≥7 a singular point would have all squares equal, hence all coordinates ±a for nonzero a, and five signs cannot sum to zero. The fifteen pairing lines are distinct. For a primitive fifth root and z ranging over its five powers, the Fourier plane is spanned by the functions z and z^(−1). It lies on S by vanishing sums of the relevant characters. To verify its orbit size in every stated characteristic, any stabilizing permutation sends z and z^(−1) to a z+b/z and c z+d/z. Pointwise product 1 and linear independence of the characters 1,z²,z^(−2) force ac=bd=0 and ad+bc=1. Thus a stabilizer is exactly a multiplication by a fifth root or such a multiplication composed with inversion, giving orbit size 120/10=12. These lines have no identically zero coordinate, so they are distinct from the pairing lines; smoothness gives completeness at 27. Frobenius sends the Fourier plane to the plane of z²,z^(−2), with disjoint projectivizations by character independence; the same holds under any common coordinate permutation. Its square preserves the plane. Thus all six pairs are nonrational and skew, and no member can contain a rational point. In the pairing arrangement, two distinct missing coordinates force a common support of size two, giving ten support-pair points each on three lines. With the same missing coordinate, the union of the two matchings is a four-cycle enforcing alternating values; there are three distinct double points per missing coordinate. There are no other meetings, so the union has 15(q+1)−20−15=15q−20 points. For the Picard calculation, the integer Gram matrix has G·1=5·1 and G²+4G=3J. The independent check /workspace/review_evidence/clebsch_gram.js, replayable with node, confirmed these identities using only the incidence rule: equal missing coordinate or a shared pair. Trace −15 gives multiplicity five for −4 and hence rank six. The line classes span a nondegenerate six-dimensional space (a seven-dimensional span would give rank seven). Frobenius fixes it and acts nontrivially on Picard since it exchanges distinct lines, which cannot be numerically equivalent by self-intersection −1 and nonnegative mutual intersection. The orthogonal complement is therefore negated. The cubic point formula gives q²+5q+1; subtraction gives (q−3)(q−7), including 0 at 7 and 60 at 13. The finite integer matrix check applies in all the stated characteristics by the proved incidence rule. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not executed; its prime-field tests would not alone establish the result or the skew conjugacy.

value.rationale: Off-line rational points are a natural arithmetic invariant of a classical cubic, and excluding all geometric lines is stronger than simply excluding known rational ones without a descent argument. The formula gives the sharp exceptional q=7 boundary and exact abundance over every admissible extension, useful when an argument requires a rational point avoiding the exceptional curves. It is not an extrapolation from a list of prime fields or just a computation of the standard Picard trace.
